16.t: Working with data: Archimedes in the lab
q: State the weight of the stone in water.
Calculate the upthrust on the steel bolt and the aluminium block.
Compare the upthrust with the weight of water displaced.
They are equal (or very close) for every object.
State the principle the data support, and suggest why the marble values differ slightly.
Archimedes’ principle: upthrust = weight of fluid displaced. The marble is tiny, so the meter’s precision (about 0.01 N) makes a small error.
